draft.title: Narratives across cultures and time
card: Every society tells stories. People have used them to pass on knowledge, values and identity, long before writing and in every culture since.
stories told aloud and handed down by memory, such as myths and fables. A fable is a short story that ends with a lesson about how to act.
stories in novels, plays and films. They reach new audiences, but they still carry ideas about what matters.
A narrative carries the beliefs of the culture that tells it. Reading a story closely can show what its people valued, feared or hoped for.
draft.remember: Stories are how cultures pass on what they know and believe, in every age.

a.q: Why have societies told stories such as myths and fables across time?
opts: To pass on knowledge, values and identity
To record exact dates of historical events
To replace the need for any spoken language
To show that all cultures hold the same beliefs
a.why: Stories let a culture hand on what it knows and believes, so each generation learns who they are. They are not exact records of events, because myths and fables often teach a lesson instead.
a.clue: Think about what a community wants its children to learn.

b.q: A fable told in a small village ends with a hare who boasts, rests and then loses a race to a slow, steady tortoise. What does this narrative most likely show about the village's culture?
opts: It values steady effort over boasting
It values speed above every other trait
It has no interest in teaching children
It copied the story from a modern film
b.why: The fable rewards the steady tortoise and punishes the boastful hare, so it carries a belief about what is worth admiring. Speed is the trait the story shows failing, so valuing speed is the tempting but wrong reading.
b.clue: Look at which animal wins and which one loses.

a.best: To pass on knowledge, values and identity

b.best: It values steady effort over boasting

proposal.title: Narratives across cultures and time
card: Every society tells stories. People have used them to pass on knowledge, values and identity, long before writing and in every culture since.
stories told aloud and handed down by memory, such as myths and fables (short stories that end with a lesson). Retold over generations, they come to reflect a whole community, not one teller.
stories in novels, plays and films. They reach new audiences, but they still carry ideas about what matters.
A narrative carries the beliefs of the culture that tells it. It is not an exact record of events, but it can show what its people valued, feared or hoped for.
proposal.remember: A story may not record what happened, but it can reveal what its culture believed.

a.q: A myth told 2,000 years ago and a film made this year are both narratives. What do they have in common?
opts: Each carries the beliefs of the culture that made it
Each is an exact record of real events of its time
Each was handed down from teller to teller by memory
Each holds values that stay the same across all ages
a.why: Every narrative, in any form or age, carries the beliefs of the culture that tells it. Being handed down by memory is a feature of oral narratives only, and a film is a screen narrative, so that option fits the myth but not the film.
a.clue: Which feature belongs to every narrative, not just one kind?

b.q: In a tale told for centuries in a fishing community, a young man ignores the elders' warning of a storm, sails out and is lost. What does the tale most likely reveal?
opts: The community valued the wisdom of its elders
A real young man drowned in a storm long ago
Every culture of that era feared the open sea
The first teller personally distrusted the young
b.why: The tale warns listeners against ignoring the elders, so it shows what the community valued. A narrative is not an exact record of events, so reading it as proof of a real drowning is the tempting mistake. Retold over generations, it reflects the community rather than one teller's views.
b.clue: Ask what the tale warns its listeners about.

a.best: Each carries the beliefs of the culture that made it

b.best: The community valued the wisdom of its elders
